title_as_printed: Comparison of the experimental solubility (in mole fraction) of methane gas in water with predictions from Henry's Law correlation at 3.45 MPa

footnotes_as_printed.*: Englezos and Bishnoi (1988), Table 1, mole fraction of methane in water at visually observed hydrate nucleation point/estimated stability limit, respectively, at 3.49 MPa.

regime_by_row.reason: 0 C is below the catastrophic temperature Tc = 2.5 C given in the text (hydrate present); 1 C row also below Tc but is literature

pressure_note: Title: 'at 3.45 MPa'; text: 'The pressure used during the experiments for pure methane is 3.45 MPa (500 psia)', constant-pressure runs (gas volume followed at fixed pressure while the liquid is cooled/heated); total vs gas partial pressure not stated.

value2.col: Mole fraction x (1000) Henry's Law prediction
value2.what: Henry's law correlation prediction at the same T and P (literature extrapolation, background for the measurements)

skip_rows.reason: no experimental value printed ('-'); only Henry's law prediction
experimental cell holds two literature values of Englezos and Bishnoi (1988) at 3.49 MPa (1.30 visually observed nucleation point / 3.26 estimated stability limit), not this work

notes: Experimental 'solubility' is derived from the volume-vs-temperature curve of a constant-pressure cooling run (values at 5-15 C are in the clear liquid before hydrate becomes visible; authors call the excess over Henry's law 'sorption'). Rows with '-' have no experimental value. Temperature is liquid temperature (PRT in the water). Experimental ramp, not static equilibrium points. Caution: the paper says Tc for ethane is 1.8 C (286.2 K), K value inconsistent.
caution: The authors call the excess over Henry law sorption: the 5-15 C values are ramped (non-equilibrium) uptake, 2-4 times the Henry baseline; the 0 C values are below the catastrophic temperature (hydrate). Not equilibrium solubilities.
